---
title: "Assessment"
subtitle: "How your grade is built — and how to do well"
---

| Component | Weight | What it involves |
|---|---|---|
| **Class participation** (in-person + online) | 30% | Cold calls, in-class problem-solving, polls and short reaction notes |
| **Short quizzes / polls** | 10% | Pre-class checks on the readings |
| **Practice-based assignment** | 20% | Case analysis or policy brief; data labs (FRED / IMF / CBN / NBS / World Bank); a country or industry macro policy memo |
| **Final exam** | 40% | On-site, closed-book examination |

## Practice-based assignments

- **Data Lab Pack** — two short labs, one graded, using FRED, IMF, CBN, NBS or World Bank data. Every session's lab on this site is good practice.
- **Case brief** — competition in platform markets ([Session 4](sessions/s04/index.qmd)) or supply-chain redesign ([Session 12](sessions/s12/index.qmd)).
- **Policy memo** — a country or sector macro strategy: a risk assessment plus an actionable playbook. Nigeria / Africa relevance is strongly encouraged. See the memo template in [Session 16](sessions/s16/index.qmd).

## How to do well in participation

1. **Read the case before class** and decide what you would recommend.
2. **Bring a number** — from the readings, the datasets or your own company.
3. **Answer the question asked**, then give your reasoning.
4. **Build on classmates** — agree, disagree or add evidence.

## The final exam

Closed-book, in class. Expect short cases that ask you to trace how a shock travels through the economy to a business, do simple calculations (real vs nominal, elasticity, debt dynamics, duration, the cost of a dollar loan), and make a recommendation. Practice questions are in [Session 16](sessions/s16/index.qmd).
